text: 🇲🇽🎨 "If public university costs money, it becomes a privilege, not a right. Only those who have the resources can pay for it. It becomes a commodity when one pays for it, and public education is a right." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Tecozautla, Hidalgo Inaugurating the Tecozautla campus of the Universidad Nacional Rosario Castellanos on October 31, Sheinbaum, 64, recalled that exactly 40 years earlier, as a UNAM physics student, she helped form the Consejo Estudiantil Universitario. The rector had approved, during the vacation period, higher tuition and fees and an end to the automatic pass from UNAM high schools into the university. Students organized from September 1986 to February 1987, struck the university and got the reforms reversed. "Since then I have always fought for public education."

🇲🇽🚁 "What profoundly distinguishes our armed forces from those of other countries is their origin. They were born of the Mexican Revolution, of the struggle to recover democracy and restore constitutional order after the coup d'état against President Francisco I. Madero." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Felipe Ángeles International Airport, State of Mexico At the 60th anniversary of Plan DN-III-E on October 30, she said their root "is in the defense of the popular will, of sovereignty and of the dignity of our people and our nation," and that its women and men "come from the people." She noted that the airport's namesake, revolutionary general Felipe Ángeles, understood "that the greatness of a man of arms is not in violence, but in his commitment to life, justice and human dignity," and quoted him: "Nothing is sacred except man." The plan has been applied in more than 87,000 emergencies since 1966.

🇲🇽🚁 "Behind every rescue, every meal delivered, every street they helped clear, there was something that does not only answer to an order from above. There was solidarity, sensitivity, love and dedication to others." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Felipe Ángeles International Airport, State of Mexico She recalled watching soldiers during the October 2025 rains that hit five states: working long days in water and mud, rescuing people, bringing food and helping communities recover their roads and homes, "with the same fervor when they support in national territory as when they are sent to other countries." The 2025 operation included the largest air bridge in the history of Plan DN-III-E. At the ceremony 869 distinctions were awarded, 833 for Plan DN-III-E work and 36 for humanitarian aid abroad.

🔥🇲🇽 "They criticized President López Obrador because he had eliminated the disaster fund. Before, they stole the money from the disaster fund. Now there are resources available and they are delivered directly." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Pachuca, Hidalgo She described the protocol now in place: Bienestar takes a census, then delivers a first, second and third support, and if a home was lost entirely, the money for the whole home. Refrigerators, stoves and other household goods went to those who lost everything. With the Pachuca handover, Hidalgo's reconstruction is closing out: roads, drinking water works and dams under way, household goods delivered, and now homes. "Nearly 8 billion pesos for the people of Hidalgo, for this very difficult moment, totally transparent and direct, through the bank of the people of Mexico, the Banco del Bienestar."

🇲🇽✊ "And what must a government do? Do what the people do: lend a hand when someone is affected. That is the lesson of the people of Mexico to the government of Mexico." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Pachuca, Hidalgo In Pachuca on October 30 she said solidarity among neighbors is "something unique to the people of Mexico," rooted in its Indigenous origin. "Unlike the past, when circumstances like these happened, they came, took a photograph and then never appeared." The October 2025 rains hit 105,000 families in Veracruz, Puebla, Querétaro, San Luis Potosí and Hidalgo. The armed forces flew food and water to cut-off communities, Bienestar census workers reached every community, and families received a first, second and third support depending on the damage while roads, bridges and water systems were rebuilt. In Hidalgo it took 40 to 50 days to reopen every road.

🇲🇽🚁 "As long as there is a family to protect, a community to aid and a Mexican who needs the support of a soldier, there will be no distance that stops us, no adversity that bends us, no risk that keeps us from our duty." — General Ricardo Trevilla Trejo, Secretary of National Defense, Felipe Ángeles International Airport On October 30 Sheinbaum led the 60th anniversary of Plan DN-III-E, the armed forces' disaster-relief plan. Created in 1965 under Defense Secretary Marcelino García Barragán and first applied in October 1966 for the Pánuco and Tamesí river floods, it has been activated in more than 87,000 emergencies, with troops acting without waiting for orders. Since 1996 Mexican military contingents have delivered humanitarian aid 99 times in 30 countries, under this administration including the United States and Venezuela. 68 soldiers have died on these missions. 869 distinctions were awarded at the ceremony.

🇲🇽✊ "The only way for the people to trust their government is for the government to trust the people of Mexico." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Pachuca, Hidalgo On October 30 in Pachuca, Sheinbaum handed Banco del Bienestar cards to 2,259 Hidalgo families who lost their homes completely in the October 2025 rains: 400,000 pesos each, on top of earlier aid, paid in three installments. That is about 900 million pesos for 228 localities in 23 municipalities. Safe land for new housing could not be found in Hidalgo's remote, steep communities, so the money goes straight to the families, who decide where and how to rebuild, whether to buy land elsewhere, and whether to hire local builders. "Who decides how it is built and where? You." Puebla and Veracruz are receiving 436 and 600 of these supports.
banner: HIDALGO FLOODS: 400K PESOS PER LOST HOME

text: 🇲🇽🎨 "There are already 120,000 students at the Rosario Castellanos, and we are going for more. We want at least double the students over the whole six-year term." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Tecozautla, Hidalgo Sheinbaum created the free public university as head of government of Mexico City (2018–2023), with six campuses in the capital. As president she made it a national university, with municipalities like Tecozautla building the facilities. Its medical schools were set up inside it rather than as a separate national health university, and one of them will be in Tecozautla, where two more buildings are planned. Students attend in person, blended or remotely: "What matters is that they have access to public education, which is a right of the people of Mexico."

🇲🇽🎨 "When public education is strengthened, violence decreases. When public education is strengthened, women's rights advance. When public education is strengthened, the country is strengthened." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Tecozautla, Hidalgo On October 31 she inaugurated the Tecozautla campus of the Universidad Nacional Rosario Castellanos, the only university in the municipality, which graduates about 1,000 high-school students a year. Classes began this October with nearly 300 students in four degrees: community tourism, medicine, administration and commerce, and law and criminology. A degree in agroecology and sustainable livestock opens in March. "That is why education, for us, is the center, the heart of the national transformation."
banner: PUBLIC EDUCATION: LESS VIOLENCE, MORE RIGHTS

🇲🇽📊 <u>Bank Lending to Mexican Businesses Picks Up: +5.6% in September</u>

Banxico data show commercial bank credit to the private sector grew 5.6% in real annual terms in September, up from 4.0% in August. Lending to companies jumped from 2.0% to 5.4%. Consumer credit grew 8.4%, and credit cards rose 12.3%.
